comments.text: BIGOTRY MAKES LIFE HARDER. Yes, the Bible explicitly commands to "love thy neighbor," appearing multiple times across both the Old and New Testaments.The phrase most commonly includes the qualifier "as thyself". The exact phrasing depends heavily on the specific Bible translation.Where to Find It in the BibleLeviticus 19:18 (Old Testament Origin): This is the very first time the command appears in scripture. In the classic King James Version (KJV), it reads: "Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord."Matthew 22:37–39 (The Gospels): When asked to name the greatest commandment in Jewish law, Jesus replies with two answers. He names loving God as the first, and says, "And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself."Mark 12:31 & Luke 10:27: These books record the exact same conversation with Jesus emphasizing that "There is none other commandment greater than these."Romans 13:9 & Galatians 5:14 (The Epistles): The Apostle Paul writes that all moral laws regarding how to treat other people are ultimately summarized into this single, core command.Who is Considered a "Neighbor"?If you read further in Luke 10, a lawyer directly asks Jesus to define who qualifies as a neighbor. Jesus responds by telling the famous Parable of the Good Samaritan.Through that story, he explains that a neighbor is not just someone who lives nearby, looks like you, or shares your religion. A neighbor is any human being you encounter who is in need of mercy and care, regardless of cultural or social boundaries.Are you looking for more context on a specific version of this story, or do you need help finding another biblical quote?
